newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maju to buy stake in steel firm for 1.02 bln rgt.
newsitem.headline: Maju to buy stake in steel firm for 1.02 bln rgt.

text.p: Malaysia's Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd has entered into a pact with steel firm Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd to buy from Perwaja a 51 percent stake in Equal Concept Sdn Bhd for 1.02 billion ringgit.
Loss-making Perwaja had been entrusted to Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd to be turned around. Equal Concept has been managing Perwaja while its privatisation plan is being worked out.

The proposed acquisition is conditional on the alloting of 2.0 billion ordinary shares in Equal Concept to Perwaja Terengganu when the restructuring and privatisation of the Perwaja group is completed, a Perwaja statement on Tuesday said.

The restructuring and privatisation involves the sale of all the subsidiaries of Perwaja Terengganu to Equal Concept for a total of 2.0 billion ringgit and the transfer of the obligations of all borrowings, loans and inter-company loans of Perwaja Terengganu's subsidiaries to Perwaja Terengganu.
The rest of the steel concern's shareholders are Lion Group with 30 percent, the government of Terengganu state with five percent and the balance with the federal government.

Malaysia's government announced earlier this year that it was assuming nearly 2.9 billion ringgit ($1.16 billion) in losses racked up by Perwaja, which is being probed by anti-corruption officials for alleged irregularities.
The company's managing director Eric Chia resigned in August 1995, and Malaysia has estimated the insolvent steel-maker would require an injection of one billion ringgit in funds to be revived.
Perwaja Terengganu said the deal with Maju was signed on May 16, 1997.
